title: Harlem jive talk
summary: Greer talks about the funny talk and slang musicians used in the 1920s; end of cassette.

blocks.x: It wasn't no all colored school. No. But I was -- we'd take white students. It was obvious. I was the only soul brother in the school band, and then we crack it down to play the basketball game, only soul brother there, so I'm out like a sore thumb, sticking out. (Laughter) One time (unintelligible) that old jive, that hip talk they call it. We called it jive. It originated in Harlem you know. We originated that. That -- we originate that. Even today, cat-all ofays, latch on, 'My man,' 'Hey daddy.' Just talking that in the 20's. We used to get around and talk

that funny talk, unless you were --you didn't know what the hell we were talking about. Talking all around, nobody knew what we were talking about -- I knew, the guys knew, because a lot of times, we'd be on the bandstand man, Hey, dig that soft, man,' -- that girl, you know, they called them softs. Dig that soft, man.' Soft times. That chick switching and don't know what the hell we're talking about.
It was funny, man, those were good days.
